references.text: The cloud that lifted from the tabernacle was the signal for the Israelites to break camp and continue their journeys; when the cloud did not lift, they did not set out.
Describes how the cloud covered the tabernacle and what it looked like at night as fire, providing context for the cloud's movements.
Elaborates on the principle that the Israelites broke camp and encamped according to the Lord's command through the movements of the cloud.
The first concrete example of the cloud lifting from the tabernacle of the testimony, and the Israelites breaking camp from the wilderness of Sinai.
The Lord went before them in a pillar of cloud by day to lead them on their way, and in a pillar of fire by night.
Nehemiah recalls how the pillar of cloud did not depart from them during the day but led them on their journey.
The psalm describes how God guided the people with the cloud by day and with the light of fire all through the night.
Paul refers to the fact that all the fathers were under the cloud, as a typology of God's guidance of His people.
